summary: Tep Bar is a compact Chinatown cultural bar pairing Thai spirits and regional small plates with live Thai music. Its current menu describes nightly performances and a two-hour minimum spend, so plan around the music and budget before arriving.
whyGo: Hear rotating ensembles using instruments including ranad ek, khim, saw u and pi chum, with contemporary interpretations of Thai traditions.
Try Thai herbal spirits, local rum and whisky in cocktails alongside regional snacks such as the giant rice cracker with sweet-spicy paste.
The Soi Nana address makes it a natural evening stop while exploring old Chinatown.
bestFor: Visitors interested in Thai music and spirits in an intimate bar setting.
Small groups who are comfortable with a lively, close-quarters evening and a minimum spend.
skipIf: You want a quiet conversation, a low-cost drink, or guaranteed seating without a spend commitment.
You need step-free access; accessible entry and facilities are not confirmed in the sources reviewed.
duration: Allow about 2 hours; the venue currently sets a two-hour dining period when there is a queue. Treat this as a planning estimate and confirm on the day.
cost: The current venue menu states a minimum spend of ฿800 per person for the two-hour period. Menu prices are subject to 10% service charge and 7% VAT; whether the minimum spend includes those additions is unclear. Check the current menu before going.
hours: The venue menu currently lists business hours 18:00–midnight and live music 20:00–23:15 daily. A Time Out Bangkok review updated 27 March 2026 lists later closing on Friday and Saturday (01:00) and earlier Saturday/Sunday opening (17:00). Confirm December hours directly.
bestTime: Arrive before the 20:00 music start for a calmer first drink and to settle in; the venue’s current menu lists performances through 23:15. The busiest period and seating availability can vary.
gettingThere: At 69–71 Soi Nana, Maitreejit Road, Pom Prap. The Tourism Authority of Thailand lists MRT Blue Line Hua Lamphong or Wat Mangkon as the nearest stations. A short taxi or walk may suit depending on your station and route; check a live map and use the exact address because this is Chinatown’s Soi Nana, not Sukhumvit’s Nana.
booking: The venue’s official site links to TableCheck reservations, and its Linktree provides reservation, map and contact links. Book ahead for a preferred time, especially on a weekend; verify the current minimum spend and cancellation terms in the booking flow.
accessibility: Step-free access, lift availability, accessible toilets and seating are not documented by the official sources reviewed. The venue is described as a small multi-level shophouse in third-party listings; contact the venue before relying on access arrangements.
practicalTips: Check the official menu and reservation page again close to your visit: spend rules, prices and hours can change.
Ask whether the ฿800 minimum is before or after service charge and VAT, and whether food and drinks both count toward it.
The room is intimate and gets busier around the live set; book and arrive early if music is your priority.
Use a taxi or rideshare for the last leg if walking through busy Chinatown streets is inconvenient.
decemberNotes: December is high season in Bangkok, so reserve ahead and allow extra time for Chinatown traffic and crowded streets. No specific December 2026 event or holiday schedule was published in the sources checked; the venue currently advertises regular nightly music, but confirm its holiday calendar and opening hours nearer the date.
uncertainties: Official venue hours (18:00–midnight daily) conflict with Time Out Bangkok’s March 2026 schedule, which gives later Friday/Saturday closing and 17:00 weekend opening.
The current ฿800 minimum spend may or may not include the stated 10% service charge and 7% VAT.
December 2026 holiday openings, performance lineup, accessibility and any age or entry conditions were not confirmed.
